title: Proposed 2027–2030 Budget
status: Proposed. Presented to Council on November 10, 2026; not yet approved.

schedule.what: Proposed budget released to Council and Calgarians; written comments and speaker registration open
Public Submissions to Council begin; Council deliberations start the week of November 23
Council approves the 2027–2030 Budget (after debate and any amendments)

headline.note: The 15% is the increase in municipal property tax revenue required from existing properties in 2027.

tax_path.source: 2027: The City of Calgary (calgary.ca/budget). 2028 to 2030: news reports of the proposed budget presented to Council on November 10, 2026 (LiveWire Calgary, Yahoo News Canada); the City's budget page gives only the 2027 figure, so treat the later years as reported, not confirmed.
tax_path.context: The City says each 1% of property tax is about $25.6 million; the 2027 increase would be the largest since 1996 (LiveWire Calgary). Calgary's five-year average increase was 3.28%, second lowest among large Canadian municipalities (LiveWire Calgary, citing the budget).

household.basis: A typical single residential property assessed at the median: $706,000 in 2026 and $688,000 in 2027. City property tax amounts are estimates, subject to final assessments. Water is a typical residential metered customer using 19 cubic metres a month.
household.source: The City of Calgary, 2027 Budget: Financial impact on Calgarians

water_2027.basis: Residential metered customer, 15 mm meter, 19 cubic metres a month
water_2027.four_year: Council approved water rates in October 2026 that raise the typical residential bill about 74% over four years (CTV News, Yahoo News Canada).
water_2027.source: The City of Calgary, 2027 water rates

comparability: The City's 2027–2030 open data counts operating spending differently from the 2023–2026 open budget (2027 shows $6.4 billion net of recoveries against $4.6 billion for 2026, with large new lines under Operational Services and Corporate Program). The City has not published a line-by-line match, so the two are not compared here.
